item.title: Austin FC suffers blowout loss to LA Galaxy in penultimate game of MLS season
item.description: AUSTIN, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 5: Ervin Torres #38 of Austin FC kicks the ball during the second half in a match against San Jose Earthquakes at Q2 Stadium on September 5, 2026 in Austin, Texas. (Photo by Noah Goldberg/Getty Images) (Noah Goldberg/Getty Images) The Apple TV broadcast Saturday momentarily panned to a shot of an Austin FC fan in the stands at Dignity Health Sports Park with a paper bag cut over his head and the word "Believed" written on it. It was a concise summary of where the club stands finishing its sixth year . As Austin FC finishes out a dreadful campaign that will see it miss the playoffs for the third time in four seasons and hit a hard reset this winter , it mercifully only has one match left following a 4-1 loss to the Los Angeles Galaxy. And while this was a game that was likely never going to be a positive for the Verde and Black considering the meaningless circumstances, it was a reminder of what's failed to materialize for Austin FC the last nine months. Here are three key takeaways from the match as Austin FC (8-15-10, 34 points, 14th West) ends the season Saturday at home against Portland. What Austin FC did well… Almost all of the positives from this game came from players 23 or younger. Ervin Torres, Jorge Alastuey and Micah Burton played well and with great effort, with Torres providing Austin FC's goal on a brilliant bending shot from 22 yards out. MORE: A nearly forgotten war is always on Oleksandr Svatok's mind Torres gave credit to Burton for his assist and noted the time the trio spent playing for Austin FC II together produced good chemistry. "I think we understand each other and what we do," said Torres, who was ranked No. 19 on the MLS' 22 under 22 list released last week. "That was a big part of it. … As young players, we especially have to show up and play our best." Austin FC interim coach Davy Arnaud noted the club needs to "get something out of the final two games" by playing young players like Torres, Alastuey, Burton and goalie Damian Las to "learn what guys are all about." It's the right move, especially in meaningless contests where a 4-1 loss is the same as a 1-0 loss. What Austin FC didn't do well… The backline was a mess, especially Ilie Sanchez and Mikkel Desler. Sanchez was slow, had a poor clearance that led to the Galaxy's first goal and was out of position on at least one more. He turns 36 in three weeks and could be entering his final game with the club. (It seems doubtful Austin FC would exercise the 2027 option on his contract, but it could roll the dice since he's on a low salary of $225,000.) In Sanchez's defense, center back is not his natural position and he just played 90 minutes Wednesday. He probably shouldn't have started and definitely shouldn't have played 75 minutes. item.title: Justin Allgaier Takes Championship Lead After Martinsville
item.description: Photo by: Greg Atkins The NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series championship battle took another dramatic turn Saturday at Martinsville Speedway, with Justin Allgaier moving into the points lead after a runner up finish and Carson Kvapil capturing the race victory. With only one race remaining in the 2026 season, five drivers remain mathematically eligible to win the championship. The penultimate race of the season delivered major consequences for the title fight. Jesse Love entered Martinsville leading the standings, but mechanical problems and a late crash completely changed the championship picture. Allgaier now heads to the season finale with control of his championship destiny, while several challengers remain close enough to make next weekend’s race at Homestead-Miami Speedway a must-watch event for NASCAR fans. He leaves Martinsville with a 22 point advantage over Love and a narrow cushion over Corey Day, who finished third. Kvapil also remains in championship contention after winning Saturday’s race. The remaining seven drivers in the Chase have been mathematically eliminated from championship contention. That group includes Sam Mayer, Sammy Smith, Taylor Gray, Brandon Jones, Austin Hill, Parker Retzlaff and Rajah Caruth. Kvapil Wins as Love Suffers Championship Setback Kvapil delivered one of the biggest performances of his season, leading 121 laps and holding off teammate Allgaier to win at Martinsville. The young driver continued to show impressive consistency and remains just 23 points behind Allgaier. He finished 30th, losing the championship lead at the worst possible time. item.title: FSU football's nightmarish season continues, loses to Clemson 36-24
item.description: Florida State football's nightmareish season continued with a 36-24 loss to Clemson in Doak Campbell Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, extending the program's losing streak to three games. With fans in costumes in the stands and festivities outside the stadium, FSU offered up little tricks or treats in another defeat for the program and head coach Mike Norvell, facing scorching pressure from the fanbase. So much so that a plane with a banner calling for his removal was flown around the stadium pregame. The loss means Norvell is now 1-5 against Dabo Swinney and Clemson as head coach with FSU. The Seminoles (3-5, 1-4 ACC) are also 10-22 dating back to the start of the 2024 season. Tiger quarterback Tait Reynolds threw for a pair of touchdowns and 189 yards. He added 85 rushing yards and a score. Ashton Daniels finished the night with three interceptions, a fumble, and 350 passing yards and two touchdowns. Here are three takeaways from the loss. Ashton Daniels's late surge can't wipe away three turnovers Daniels turned the ball over four times, fittingly handing them out to the Tigers' defense like Halloween candy. He threw a pair of interceptions into double coverage in the first half and coughed up a fumble late in the third quarter on a fourth-down attempt when FSU was in the red zone, aiming to cut into a 26-10 deficit. He had reached the line to gain, but Derian Mayo stripped him, and the ball fell into the grateful hands of Jahiem Lawson. In the fourth quarter, he came up with two touchdowns, one through the air, a 41-yard strike to Jasen Lopez, and one on the ground, a 13-yard scamper. However, with the ball on the nine-yard line late in the fourth, he threw his third interception, which ended the game. Daniels was sacked four times, and critically, wasn't allowed success running the football until late in the fourth quarter. FSU's offense operates at its best when he can run, and the Tigers kept him quiet until his 13-yard touchdown run that cut the score to 29-18 after a two-point conversion in the fourth quarter. Wounded FSU offense mostly stuck in neutral Daniels and the slow offensive start weren't aided by a run game that never got going. Without Ousmane Kromah and Samuel Singleton Jr., the rushing attack was always going to struggle. Tre Wisner and Daniels struggled against the Clemson front seven. FSU rushed for 2.2 yards per carry and finished with a season-low 65 total rushing yards. The Seminoles offense had such a slow start that it took four drives to record a first down, which came on a generous pass interference call. The offense did cash in on the next play as Daniels uncorked a 46-yard touchdown pass to Micahi Danzy. It was the biggest, and arguably the only play of note in the first half. FSU recorded 133 yards in the first half, with 98 through the air and 35 on the ground. The Seminoles finished the night with 415 and went 1-of-10 on third down. item.title: Brewers stars go trick-or-treating in Wauwatosa, pose for selfies
item.description: Three blocks from her house, while trick-or-treating, Lindsay Emer and the rest of her group stopped walking and started running. They needed to get back to their street. Quickly. Seconds earlier, one of Emer's neighbors, Stacie Ardoin, had sent a message to the neighbor group chat. Most of the trick-or-treaters, including Emer, didn't see it. One person did. She looked down at her phone and saw Ardoin sent a picture. "I think the Brewers are on our block," Emer's friend told the group after looking at the photo. She turned her phone around, showing everyone what Ardoin sent. It was a selfie, her standing next to trick-or-treaters. Who just so happened to be Jake Bauers, Andrew Vaughn, Grant Anderson, DL Hall and Sal Frelick. Three days after winning the World Series, and one day after throwing the biggest party Wisconsin has ever seen , these MLB champions were trick-or-treating. Everyone in the group − yes, even the children − agreed. A picture with the Milwaukee Brewers trumped any amount of candy they could get. "Immediately it was like, 'All right, we got to go,'" Mike Emer, Lindsay's husband told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel. They started running back to Auburn Avenue in Wauwatosa, between 70th and 72nd street, where they all live. A couple minutes later, they made it, slowing down when they got close to meet them as normal as possible. Buy Brewers World Series championship T-shirts, hats, gear, merch Frelick and Vaughn were matching beer mugs. Hall was an astronaut. Bauers and Anderson didn't dress up. Vaughn and Bauers were both with their kids. "Word on the street is that Vaughn lives in our neighborhood," Lindsay, 42, said. "But I can't confirm that." The players happily obliged requests to take photos with both the adults and children. Lindsay got one with her, her 8-year-old daughter Scarlett, and Frelick. Then, Vaughn got in the frame for a second. Isaac, Lindsay's 6-year-old son, got one with Bauers, and another with Hall and Vaughn. "They were really nice. Very laid back," Lindsay said. "They just seemed like they were doing their thing and being parents, and were very sweet when we asked for a couple of photos." Hoping to let the players trick-or-treat in peace, Lindsay kept the interaction brief, and not inundating them with questions. Mike asked one, to Frelick, about how he was doing on his proclamation to drink 100,000 beers. "I'm working on it," Frelick responded, not specifying a remaining number. item.title: Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith breaks Big Ten all-time receiving TD record
item.description: Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has broken the all-time Big Ten receiving touchdowns record of 39 previously held by Michigan's Braylon Edwards. Smith set the new mark after a touchdown catch in the fourth quarter against USC on Oct. 31. Smith entered the game needing one touchdown to pass Edwards, who set the record in 2004. Smith set the Ohio State touchdown record in the Buckeyes' win over Iowa on Sept. 19, a record previously held by Chris Olave. If he forgoes his last year of college eligibility after the 2026 season, Smith is expected to be one of the top picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. While the regular season has arrived, the eligibility battles on the court haven’t stopped. Fifth-year transfers Keyshawn Hall and Reed Bailey, as well as former G-Leaguer Babacar Sane, are still awaiting full NCAA clearance. item.description: Another tough first period and more offensive struggles have the Blue Jackets flying home unhappy after a 3-1 loss to the Dallas Stars on Oct. 31 at American Airlines Center in Dallas, Texas. More: Zach Werenski's goal drought is an issue for the Columbus Blue Jackets Damon Severson scored the only goal for the Blue Jackets (5-7-0), who finished their first multi-game road trip with a 1-2-0 record. Jet Greaves made 14 saves on 16 shots but his second goal allowed was tough to swallow after it gave the Stars a 2-0 lead with 0.2 seconds left in the first period. Mikko Rantanen and Thomas Harley gave the Stars (8-5-1) a 2-0 lead in the first and Arttu Hyry scored into an empty net with 0.3 left in the third to seal the goaltending win for Jake Oettinger, who made five of his 25 saves to keep the Jackets from tying it in the final 11-plus minutes. A buzzer beater from Harls pic.twitter.com/HaBnh8ZQpS — Dallas Stars (@DallasStars) November 1, 2026 Turning point Already trailing 1-0 on Rantanen's early power-play goal, the Blue Jackets took a gut punch right before going to the locker room for the first intermission. item.description: Golden State's Gabby Williams scored 30 points to lead the Valkyries over Atlanta in the deciding seventh game of the WNBA Finals to earn the series MVP award (EZRA SHAW) Gabby Williams scored 30 points and the Golden State Valkyries captured their first Women's NBA title on Saturday, defeating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in a winner-take-all championship showdown. Williams scored a WNBA Finals one-half record 28 points in the second half as the second-year expansion Valkyries won the series four games to three, the longest title matchup in league history. "I wasn't going to lose on Halloween," Williams said. "It's easy when the energy is this good and positive. I wouldn't change a thing." Despite only two points in the first half, Williams seized command in the second with the game on the line and lifted Golden State ahead to stay in the dying minutes to earn the WNBA Finals Most Valuable Player award. "I just, I don't know. I love moments like this," Williams said. "Nat (coach Natalie Nakase) told me to be patient in the first half. It was hard but I listened to her and she was right as always." "All it took was good people. We have winners. "We have people who are ready to put their bodies on the floor to win a game. They don't care about scoring. They just want to do defense and rebounding. Do whatever it takes and we built a beautiful culture here." The victory came before a sellout crowd of more than 18,000 at the Chase Center that cheered the home side to a crown as the Dream lost the finals for the fourth time in the team's 18-year history. "We have an incredible team. What you did was unbelievable," team owner Joe Lacob said. Williams sank a three-pointer with 2:19 remaining to give Golden State a 60-57 lead and after Atlanta's Allisha Gray missed a layup added two free throws for a five-point edge. Kiah Stokes put back a Williams miss for a 64-57 lead and free throws by Tiffany Hayes and Veronica Burton down the stretch sealed the victory. "This is for all the people that have been underrated, misunderstood," Nakase said. "This is proof that if you put in all your heart and all your soul you can ... win championships." Golden State seized an 8-0 lead as the Dream missed their first nine shots. Atlanta answered with a 21-6 run to seize the lead, starting the second quarter with a 9-0 streak on the way to a 30-24 halftime lead. item.description: The Golden State Valkyries brought to a conclusion a WNBA season that shattered viewership and attendance records with their first WNBA championship Saturday in a thrilling 68-63 victory over the Atlanta Dream in Game 7. Golden State star Gabby Williams paced the Valkyries with 30 points, 4 blocks and 3 steals in 38 minutes. "All we heard last year: We don't have no stars, we don't have no talent," Williams said after the game. "Yeah right. We got good people. We got winners." Jordin Canada led the Atlanta Dream in scoring with 18 points, adding 5 assists and 4 rebounds. Atlanta superstar Angel Reese struggled throughout the game, finishing with 8 points on 3-of-7 shooting in 33 minutes. The victory was the first for a team in a Game 7. The league transitioned from a five-game series to a seven-game series starting last year. This is the first title for the Valkyries in just their second season as a team. And the Dream are now winless in four WNBA Finals appearances. The 2026 season was an unqualified success for the WNBA. The league set a new attendance record with 3.8 million fans attending 330 regular season games, according to the WNBA . The league said average attendance was up 21% from last year's record high. ESPN, ABC and CBS all delivered their most-watched seasons in history, according to the WNBA. The league had three times as many games averaging at least 1 million viewers as the previous record set last year. How they got here The Valkyries, despite having just one All-Star, took a major leap in just their second year in the league. The team is owned by Joe Lacob and Peter Guber, who also own the Golden State Warriors. The team quickly became relevant, going 23-21 in their first year in existence before losing in the first round of the playoffs. The signing of Gabby Williams in the offseason propelled the team to even greater success. The Valkyries went 32-12 in the regular season and beat the Paige Bueckers-led Dallas Wings and A'ja Wilson-led Las Vegas Aces to advance to the title series. The Dream didn't lose a game on its path to the title series, defeating the Kiki Iriafen-led Washington Mystics and the Breanna Stewart-led New York Liberty in sweeps. The Valkyries won Game 1 at home, 68-64, behind 26 points from Williams. Atlanta dominated the next two games behind all-time great performances from star Angel Reese. The Dream star posted 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 and 21 points and 12 rebounds in Game 3. Reese struggled to score in Games 4 and 5, shooting just 4-of-20 with 15 points combined, as the Valkyries wrestled control of the series away from the Dream. The Dream plays its regular season games at Gateway Center Arena, but its capacity is just 3,500 compared to about 17,000 at State Farm Arena.
